events.rationale: The page heading still introduces production deployment options.

The original warning is split and expanded: production explicitly includes private or single-user deployments, and security and stability concerns join scaling; debugger and reloader restrictions are added.
Self-hosted options retain the same subject despite capitalization and relocation.

The WSGI application definition and guidance for unlisted servers are split across two paragraphs; HTTP-to-WSGI translation is explained and server-selection advice replaces consulting an unlisted server manual.
Adds an explicit explanation of the documentation scope and the range of server configurations.
Adds the reverse-proxy definition and reasons to put a dedicated HTTP server before WSGI.
Renamed and relocated heading for externally hosted deployment options.
Adds what managed hosting provides, potential free-tier limits, and its relation to WSGI servers.
The PythonAnywhere hosting option is relocated and its visible label shortened.
The same Google App Engine hosting option has a shorter visible label.
Adds Google Cloud Run as a named hosting option.
The same AWS Elastic Beanstalk hosting option has a shorter visible label.
Both labels refer to Azure, but removing the IIS qualifier could be a shortened label or a scope change. Excluded link destinations cannot settle that distinction.
Adds caveats about the non-exhaustive platform list and selection based on pricing, features, and support.
Adds a proxy-fix recommendation for most hosting platforms.
Heroku is no longer listed among the hosting options.

review_notes: Independently read all old and new extracted passages before any model predictions. All correspondences and statuses retained.
Retained old [1] -> new [1, 2] as modified: the warning is expanded to debugger/reloader, private deployments, and stability/security.

Retained old [2] -> new [4, 7] as modified: its WSGI identity and unlisted-server advice are distributed across a definition and revised selection guidance. Fine-grained links remain a human-review judgment.
Retained Azure old [7] -> new [14] as uncertain: the removed IIS qualifier could reflect broader scope or merely a shorter link label.
